project_brief.title: Interactive Portfolio with Embedded Game
project_brief.description: Build a personal portfolio website that showcases your projects and includes a playable game (e.g., memory match, snake, or simple platformer) embedded directly into the page. The portfolio will be fully responsive and the game will be built with vanilla JavaScript or a lightweight library like Phaser. This project demonstrates front-end development skills, interactive design, and game logic implementation.
key_features: Responsive portfolio layout with project cards and about section
Embedded interactive game (e.g., memory match, snake, or simple platformer)
Deployed on GitHub Pages or Netlify

step_by_step_build_guide.title: Project Setup and HTML Structure
step_by_step_build_guide.engineering_action: Initialize Git repository, create project folder structure, write basic HTML skeleton with semantic elements, link external CSS and JavaScript files, and set up a local development server.
step_by_step_build_guide.required_prereq_knowledge: Basic understanding of HTML tags, CSS linking, and Git commands (init, add, commit).

step_by_step_build_guide.title: Responsive Layout with CSS Grid and Flexbox
step_by_step_build_guide.engineering_action: Build a responsive portfolio layout using CSS Grid for the overall page structure and Flexbox for aligning project cards, about section, and navigation. Ensure the design adapts to different screen sizes.
step_by_step_build_guide.required_prereq_knowledge: CSS selectors, box model, media queries, and basic layout principles.

step_by_step_build_guide.title: Interactive Elements and Event Handling
step_by_step_build_guide.engineering_action: Add JavaScript interactivity: implement smooth scrolling, project card hover effects, a modal for project details, and a responsive navigation menu. Use event listeners for user interactions.
step_by_step_build_guide.required_prereq_knowledge: JavaScript basics (variables, functions, DOM manipulation), event handling, and CSS transitions.

step_by_step_build_guide.title: Game Development with Canvas and Game Loop
step_by_step_build_guide.engineering_action: Implement a simple game (e.g., memory match, snake, or basic platformer) using the HTML5 Canvas API. Create a game loop that updates game state and renders graphics. Handle keyboard or mouse input for player control.
step_by_step_build_guide.required_prereq_knowledge: JavaScript objects, functions, Canvas API basics (drawing shapes, images), and understanding of game loops.

step_by_step_build_guide.title: Game State Management and Polish
step_by_step_build_guide.engineering_action: Add game state management: score, lives, levels, and game-over conditions. Implement smooth animations, transitions, and optional sound effects. Embed the game into the portfolio page and ensure it works seamlessly.
step_by_step_build_guide.required_prereq_knowledge: State management patterns, animation techniques (requestAnimationFrame), and event handling for game input.

step_by_step_build_guide.title: Contact Form and Deployment
step_by_step_build_guide.engineering_action: Build a contact form with HTML5 validation (required fields, email format) and JavaScript validation for custom rules. Style the form to match the portfolio. Deploy the project to GitHub Pages or Netlify. Perform final testing and polish.
step_by_step_build_guide.required_prereq_knowledge: HTML forms, form validation, basic JavaScript, and deployment process (GitHub Pages or Netlify).

tradeoffs_noted: Time conflict: project needs ~90h (6w × 15h/w baseline), learner has 32h (4h/w × 8w). Deficit: 58h (64% short).
(a) Scope reduced: focus on core feature module only, defer UI polish & caching.
(c) Scaffold provided: pre-built boilerplate for transport/data layer, learner focuses on business logic.

execution_model: Product-First Build Guide → Reverse Knowledge Mapping (25-Min Tasks)

rubric.functional_correctness: Code runs and satisfies deliverable acceptance criteria
rubric.language_syntax_idiom: Code adheres to standard HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6), Canvas API, Phaser.js (optional), Git, GitHub Pages conventions
rubric.error_handling: Code handles exceptions, network loss, and edge cases
